questions.title: How does the DPO loss (Eq. 12) derive from the Bradley‑Terry model without the partition function?
questions.question_body:
In Section 4 the authors rewrite the Bradley‑Terry preference probability in terms of the optimal policy $
abla$ (Eq. 9) and claim that the partition function $Z(x)$ cancels out when substituting the reparameterization of the reward (Eq. 7). I tried to do the algebra myself but keep ending up with a residual $\log Z(x)$ term. Could someone walk through the derivation step‑by‑step, showing explicitly how the $Z(x)$ term disappears and why this is valid under the Bradley‑Terry model?

questions.title: Why is $ eta$ interpreted as a KL‑constraint strength rather than a temperature?
questions.question_body: The paper introduces $ eta$ in Eq. (3) as the coefficient of the KL divergence regularizer and later uses it in the DPO objective (Eq. 12) inside a logistic. In many RL‑HF works $ eta$ is called a temperature controlling stochasticity of the policy. How should I think about $ eta$ in DPO – is it a temperature, a KL penalty weight, or both? How does changing $ eta$ affect the trade‑off between reward maximisation and staying close to the reference policy?

questions.title:
What exactly is meant by “reference policy” $
abla_{ref}$ and how is it obtained when no SFT model exists?
questions.question_body:
The DPO algorithm requires a reference policy $
abla_{ref}$ for computing importance weights (Eq. 12). The paper says to set $
abla_{ref}=\pi^{SFT}$ if available, otherwise to train it by maximum likelihood on preferred completions $y_w$. Could you clarify why training on only $y_w$ yields a good approximation of the original SFT distribution, and what practical differences arise if we instead use a randomly initialized model as $
abla_{ref}$?

questions.title: How does the gradient weighting term $\,\sigma(\,\hat r_	heta(x,y_l)-\hat r_	heta(x,y_w))$ prevent model degeneration?
questions.question_body: In Eq. (13) the authors note that an unweighted version of the update leads to degeneration (Appendix Table X). Intuitively I see that examples where the model already ranks $y_w$ higher receive a smaller weight, but I’m not clear on why this weighting is crucial for stability. Can anyone explain how this factor influences variance of updates or prevents collapse to trivial solutions?

questions.title: Does DPO guarantee convergence to the same optimal policy as RLHF with PPO?
questions.question_body: Both DPO and PPO optimise Eq. (3) under the same KL constraint, yet DPO replaces RL with a cross‑entropy loss. Under what assumptions (e.g., expressive policy class, exact gradient estimation) can we guarantee that DPO will converge to the same optimum as PPO? Are there known cases where DPO could get stuck in a suboptimal stationary point while PPO would not?

questions.title:
How does DPO handle multi‑token sequences when computing $
abla_{	heta}\log \pi(y\mid x)$?
questions.question_body: The loss involves log‑probabilities of whole completions $y$. Practically, language models factorise $\pi(y\mid x)=\prod_t \pi(y_t\mid x, y_{<t})$. When back‑propagating through Eq. (12), are all token probabilities weighted equally by the importance term, or is there any per‑token weighting? Does this affect training stability for long generations?

questions.title: What are the theoretical implications of Lemma 2 (same optimal policy for equivalent rewards)?
questions.question_body: Lemma 2 states that reward functions differing by a function of $x$ only produce identical optimal policies under the KL‑constrained objective. How does this fact justify discarding absolute reward scaling during training? Does it imply that any additive constant to $r(x,y)$ is irrelevant for learning, and why does this matter for DPO’s reparameterisation?

questions.title: Can DPO be combined with off‑policy preference data (e.g., collected from older models)?
questions.question_body:
The paper mentions that preference datasets are typically collected from a fixed SFT model and that DPO uses that model as $
abla_{ref}$. If I have a mixture of preferences generated by several historic policies, how should I choose or construct $
abla_{ref}$? Is there a principled way to weight different reference policies within DPO?

questions.title: Why does DPO appear more robust to sampling temperature than PPO in the TL;DR experiments?
questions.question_body: Figure 2 shows DPO’s win rate remains high across temperatures while PPO’s degrades sharply at higher temperatures. Is this robustness an intrinsic property of the DPO objective, or could it be due to differences in how temperature interacts with KL regularisation during training? What mechanisms could explain this behaviour?

questions.title: How would one extend DPO to multi‑turn dialogue where preferences depend on entire conversation histories?
questions.question_body: The current formulation assumes independent $(x, y)$ pairs and binary preferences between two completions. For multi‑turn dialogue, preferences may involve sequences of turns. How can the DPO loss be adapted to handle such sequential preference data? Would we need a different preference model (e.g., Plackett‑Luce over trajectories) or can we still use Eq. (12) with minor modifications?
